subject: System Design
title: Time-Series Databases
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Time-Series Databases.

hook.text: A monitoring system ingests 10 million metrics per second. Traditional databases buckle under that write load.

buildup.text: Time-series databases like InfluxDB and TimescaleDB are optimized for timestamped, append-only data.

discovery.text: They automatically compress old data and support downsampling: keeping hourly averages instead of per-second data.

twist.text: Time-series databases aren't general purpose. They're terrible at random updates or complex relational queries.

climax.text: For IoT sensors, server metrics, and financial ticks, time-series databases outperform general databases by 100x.

punchline.text: Purpose-built for data that flows with time.

quiz.question: What makes time-series databases different?
options: Optimized for timestamped, append-only data with automatic compression
